title: Check if One String Swap Can Make Strings Equal
spaceBreakdown:
- int first, second, n, i: scalars → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input strings s1, s2
approach: Scan both strings once, collecting indices where s1[i] != s2[i]. If there are zero mismatches the strings are already equal (zero swaps needed). If there are exactly two mismatches at indices i and j, a single swap fixes them iff s1[i] == s2[j] and s1[j] == s2[i]. Any other count of mismatches is impossible to fix with at most one swap. This is correct because one swap touches at most two positions, so it can repair at most two mismatches, and the swapped characters must land in the right spots.
hints: When two equal-length strings differ, a single swap on one string can change at most two positions. What counts of differing positions are therefore even theoretically repairable by one swap?
Linear scan collecting mismatch indices. For s1="bank", s2="kanb", mismatches are at indices 0 and 3; verify s1[0]=='b'==s2[3] and s1[3]=='k'==s2[0].

```
diffs = []
for i in 0..n-1:
    if s1[i] != s2[i]:
        diffs.append(i)
if len(diffs) == 0: return true
if len(diffs) != 2: return false
return s1[diffs[0]] == s2[diffs[1]] and s1[diffs[1]] == s2[diffs[0]]
```

**Single mismatch** - only one position differs, but one swap always touches two positions.
`Input: s1 = "a", s2 = "b"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning true whenever mismatches <= 2 without checking the count is exactly 0 or 2 → returns true

**Already equal** - zero swaps needed.
`Input: s1 = "kelb", s2 = "kelb"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: requiring exactly two mismatches (returning false when diffs is empty) → returns false

**Three mismatches** - one swap cannot fix three positions.
`Input: s1 = "abc", s2 = "def"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: only checking the swap condition on the first two mismatches and ignoring the third → returns true

**Wrong pairing** - two mismatches but characters don't cross-match.
`Input: s1 = "ab", s2 = "ca"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking only s1[diffs[0]] == s2[diffs[1]] without also checking s1[diffs[1]] == s2[diffs[0]] → returns true

followUps.q: What if you are allowed up to k swaps on s1 instead of just one?
followUps.a: Count mismatches; each swap fixes at most two, so you need ceil(mismatches/2) <= k, and the multiset of characters in s1 must equal the multiset in s2. Time O(n), space O(1) since alphabet is 26 letters.

followUps.q: What if strings can be up to 10^7 length and arrive as a stream?
followUps.a: Keep a running list of up to 3 mismatch indices; the moment a third mismatch appears you can early-return false. Otherwise finish the stream and apply the same 0-or-2 check. Time O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if a swap can exchange one character from s1 with one character from s2 (cross-string swap)?
followUps.a: The condition changes: for two mismatches i, j you need s1[i]==s1[j] and s2[i]==s2[j] (so the cross-swap lands each character correctly), plus the zero-mismatch case still returns true. Time O(n), space O(1).
